# Orbit feature checklist

Every row is one behaviour from the clean-room spec. Status per ID: **spec’d** (every row) → **built** → **tested** (a unit or e2e test names the ID) → **feels right** (lead sign-off after a hands-on review against `feel.md`).

**Totals:** 472 spec’d · 247 built (85 partial) · 337 tested · 0 feel right. 13 more are out of scope and not counted.

P0 = milestone-1 core experience, P1 = parity, P2 = later.

## Page navigation, windows, links and page-level controls (prefix NV)

Spec: `spec/navigation.md`

| ID | Feature | P | Built | Tested | Feels right | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| NV-01 | Back and forward | P0 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | – | buttons and keys (Cmd+Left/Right only outside text fields), history menu with favicons that closes on tab switch, Cmd/middle-click opens the entry in a background tab with its history; mouse side buttons are Chromium's; Backspace inert |
| NV-02 | Trackpad two-finger swipe back/forward | P1 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | – | a horizontal two-finger swipe over the page goes back or forward: an arrow slides in from that edge of the page's card, following the fingers 1:1, fills once it's fully in (112 px), and letting go then goes as Back and Forward do; let go sooner, it fades and nothing happens. Only with somewhere to go, and on macOS only with the system's Swipe between pages on. The page gets the swipe first: while what's under the pointer (or around it) can still scroll that way, or the page uses the wheel (preventDefault), the swipe is the page's until the fingers lift, so it navigates only at the scroll edge. Over the sidebar the same swipe switches Space (SP-08) and never navigates. Windows and Linux: wherever the touchpad scrolls smoothly (pixel deltas); a mouse wheel's notches never navigate. Recognition follows the Space swipe (FL-13): 9 px decide the axis, and the fingers have lifted after a 90 ms pause or when the OS momentum starts. Limits: Electron reports no scroll phases, so the page preload watches the page's wheel events in its own world (D40 use orbit-page:swipe); the swipe goes by the scroll's direction, so with macOS's natural scrolling off a swipe right is forward; a swipe that starts over a frame of the page stays the frame's (frames get no preload); the arrow's small view takes the wheel if the pointer is right over it. Tests use synthetic trackpad scrolls; the real gesture, with momentum, is unverified on macOS (person-check) |
| NV-03 | Reload and hard reload | P0 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | – | Cmd/Ctrl+R, F5; hard reload Cmd+Shift+R, Ctrl+Shift+R, Shift+F5, Ctrl+F5; Cmd/middle-click Reload duplicates with history; keyboard focus goes to the page |

| NV-05 | Find in page | P0 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | – | floating bar over the active page's top-right corner; finds as you type, n/m count, No matches; Enter/Cmd+G/F3 next, Shift+Enter/Shift+Cmd+G/Shift+F3 previous, buttons; Esc closes and keeps the match selected; per tab (hidden on switch, back with text and place); starts from the selection, else the last search; IME commits; keys typed for the bar before it has the keyboard (a new window's first moments, a busy bar) wait up to 5 s and then go into it in order, text as text (any character); it takes the keyboard when it shows, even later than that; shortcuts and IME composition are not held; Cmd+J jumps to the selection (macOS); Edit > Find menu; does nothing while a Peek is open, so the keyboard stays in it (finding in a Peek is PK-11) |
| NV-06 | Page zoom | P0 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | – | Chromium steps 25-500% on Cmd+=/Cmd+-/Cmd+0 and Ctrl+wheel (Win/Linux), in a Peek (with a toast) and a Mini Window (no indicator there) too; per host in each profile (all its tabs), remembered across launches (written on quit), dropped with a deleted profile; indicator with Reset over the page for 1.5 s (longer while hovered); pinch is visual zoom and Cmd+0 undoes it too |

Differences: window.print() returns at once and the page goes on (Chromium's waits for the dialog); a frame's own window.print() opens the system's print dialog (frames have no preload, D40); no paper size, margins, scale, pages per sheet or two-sided choices (the preview and PDF are A4, or Letter where the region uses it; a printer uses its own paper); a page may call print() again as soon as its dialog closes. Tests print and save nothing (the one function that sends a job out records it, and the printers come from ORBIT_E2E_PRINTERS); only a person can check that a real printer prints what the preview shows, and Save as PDF's save dialog |

| NV-20 | Full screen | P1 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | – | ⌃⌘F on macOS (fn+F / Globe+F is the system's own key and does the same), F11 and Alt+Shift+F on Windows and Linux, View → Toggle Full Screen (macOS) and the command bar toggle window full screen; a held key toggles once. In full screen the sidebar hides and the page fills the window; the window's left edge brings the sidebar in over the page (SB-12), and the loading indicator stays (SB-28). Leaving docks the sidebar again, unless the user docked or hid it meanwhile (⌘S); a window closed or quit in full screen keeps its docked sidebar for next time; a window opened from one in full screen opens in full screen, its sidebar hidden (NV-10). Esc in a page, or over its error or crash screen, goes to the page first and full screen stays; pressed again within a second, or held (at its first repeat), it leaves full screen, and the page gets neither that press nor its repeats (nor, as the engine does after a key it didn't deliver, the release); presses further apart each go to the page. A single Esc never leaves, even one the page left alone: nothing asks the page (D60), and a web app's Esc is often its own without preventDefault. Exit Full Screen in Settings → Shortcuts prefers websites by default; set to prefer Orbit, one Esc leaves at once and the page gets nothing of it (KS-02, D68). Esc is no binding of it: an open overlay (command bar, Peek, find bar, a page dialog) takes Esc first (KS-19). The Esc that leaves full screen on a loading page doesn't stop the load (NV-04). A video's own full screen is Chromium's: it fills the window without the sidebar, Esc leaves only it, and the toggle keys leave both. Mini Windows don't go full screen this way. Xvfb has no window manager, so the e2e tests check the state and layout Orbit keeps; a person checks that the window really fills the screen, the macOS animation (the sidebar goes and comes back as it ends), fn+F / Globe+F, and that the View menu has one full-screen item (macOS may add its own Enter Full Screen beside Orbit's). Known limits (keys lane): with the keyboard in a frame of a loading page, the Esc the page gets stops the load after 250 ms, as only the main frame answers (K5); the first key right after the keyboard moves into a frame can come before that frame says where its keyboard is (K7) |
| NV-21 | Save page and view source | P2 | ✅ | ✅ e2e | – | Save Page As…: ⇧⌘S (Ctrl+Shift+S on Windows and Linux; ⌘S is the sidebar's, SB-11), File → Save As… (macOS menu), the command bar's Save Page As… and the page menu's, each showing its live keys (KS-18). The OS save dialog opens from the Downloads folder, named after the page: a web page saves as a single file (MHTML) or, named .html, as its HTML alone; a local page whose frames are all local files saves complete (D49). A Peek's or a Mini Window's page saves itself. View Source is DT-04. On a canvas tab the same command exports the canvas: that comes with EZ-11 (no canvases yet). |
| NV-22 | Translate a page | P2 | ⛔ out of scope | – | – | Orbit's engine has no built-in translation, and the spec allows no paid API (D45). ST-14's offer to translate, the Translate command and the address field's translate button go with it |
| NV-23 | Reader mode | P2 | – | – | – |  |
| NV-24 | Page dialogs (alert, confirm, prompt, leave-page, sign-in, file pickers) | P1 | 🟡 partial | ✅ e2e+unit | – | alert, confirm and prompt show Orbit's own dialog over that page only (a tab, a split view pane, a Peek, a Mini Window, a pop-up): the sidebar, other tabs and the command bar stay usable, a tab's dialog waits while another tab shows and shows again on return, Enter answers, Esc cancels (closes an alert), Tab stays in the dialog, and the page gets the keyboard back; the page's text shows as text, cut at 10,000 characters; "Leave site?" ("Reload site?" for a reload) when a page that asks for it, after a user gesture as in Chromium, goes: a link, a form or location, Orbit's address, Back, Forward or Reload (Leave starts it again), closing its tab (shown first; Cancel keeps it) or its window (Cancel keeps it), a pop-up's window; a page's own history.back() or a frame's navigation it stopped goes on at the user's next try within 10 s; auto-archive and sleep keep a tab whose page warns, or waits on its dialog, until the user closes it; HTTP sign-in (Basic, Digest; a server or a proxy) over the page, Cancel shows the server's own page; file, folder, colour and date pickers are the engine's own (not run in tests: they wait for a person); a dialog a frame asks for is Electron's: alert and confirm in its own message box, not over the page, and prompt returns null (the preload runs in main frames only, D40); quitting doesn't ask; closing a Peek or a Mini Window doesn't ask yet (their close paths are the finish-views lane's) |
| NV-25 | Share the current page | P2 | – | – | – |  |

Spec: `spec/archive.md`

| ID | Feature | P | Built | Tested | Feels right | Notes |

| AR-01 | What goes into the Archive | P0 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | – | close, auto-archive, Clear, archive-below, pinned/folder/Space delete, Mini Window and Peek pages; entries carry tab, Space name, section, reason; back/forward history kept outside OrbitState (userData/archive, page state in memory only); private and empty tabs never archived; state keeps the newest ~200-300, the rest lives in the Archive store |
| AR-02 | Where the Archive lives and how to open it | P0 | ✅ | ✅ e2e | – | Library view over the page area (its own view above the tabs, below the command bar and Peek) from the bottom-bar button, ⌘⇧L (Open Library), ⌘T View Archive / Open Library and the macOS Archive menu; reopens to the last section; Esc, ⌘W or selecting another tab closes it and the page gets the keys back; section registry (*.library-section.tsx) for other lanes |
| AR-03 | Archive list layout | P0 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | – | newest first under Today / Yesterday / date headings; favicon, title, host, time and origin-Space badge; filters by source (all, sidebar, Mini Window), Space and how it closed; per profile (PR-05); virtualised and paged, fast at 10k entries. A row click previews (AR-06); ⌘-click and ⇧-click select |
| AR-04 | Search the Archive | P0 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | – | search field filters on each keystroke (title and URL, case-insensitive, partial words, every word) using the Archive store's keys (history queryTerms/urlKeyOf); typing on narrows the last answer; Enter restores and shows the top or highlighted match; ⌘F focuses it. The command bar's Archived results search the whole Archive store of the profile, not only the recent entries kept in state |
| AR-05 | Restore an archived tab | P0 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | – | Restore (hover button, Enter, row menu, several selected) puts tabs at the top of their Space's Today in order, with their tab id and back/forward history when the profile matches (never across profiles); routing rule > origin Space > current Space; toast with Go to Space when it lands elsewhere; command bar restores without a jump. A row click previews (AR-06) instead of restoring. Undoing Delete Folder after the Space changed profile also follows the new profile (W3) |
| AR-06 | Preview an archived item without restoring | P2 | 🟡 partial | ✅ e2e+unit | – | a row click opens its page in a Peek over the Library (the Peek component, its open and close motion); the entry stays archived. ⌘W and Esc close only the Peek and the Library takes the keys back (Enter then restores that row); Open as Tab (⌘O) opens it as a tab and keeps the entry; closing a preview, or a reopen of it, archives no second entry. Missing: a Restore button in the Peek card (peek lane). The Peek carries overlay.archiveEntry and archive.restorePreview restores and closes it. With no tab to preview over (an empty Space), a click opens the page in a new tab |
| AR-07 | Clear the Archive | P1 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | – | Clear Archive… from the Archive entry’s right-click menu in the Library, Archive → Clear Archive… (macOS app menu) and the command bar; always asks in the Library first (Cancel has the focus, Esc cancels), says it can’t be undone and that browsing history is kept; clears the profile shown, and the cleared pages leave the disk at once (the log is rewritten). Delete (a row’s menu, or Delete for the selected rows) shows a toast whose Undo puts the entries back with their history for a minute |
| AR-08 | Retention of archived entries | P1 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | – | settings.archiveKeepDays, default 30; 30 Days / 90 Days / 1 Year / Forever from the Archive entry’s menu in the Library and Archive → Keep Archived Tabs For (macOS) until Settings exist. A shorter time that would delete entries asks first, in the Library, saying how many (Cancel keeps them all and the time as it was). Purged once the Archive is read at launch, hourly, and at once when a shorter time is confirmed; browsing history is not touched |
| AR-09 | Reopen recently closed tabs | P0 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | – | ⌘⇧T and ⌘Z walk back through closes with full history (TB-07, TB-18); ⌘Z also shows the tab again when it was the one shown; a closed Peek comes back through the same key (PK-10, peek lane). A page closed in the last 10 minutes keeps its history rank in the command bar (as the archived row). macOS File menu: Reopen Closed Tab and a Recently Closed submenu of the last 10; on every platform the Archive toolbar has a Recently Closed menu. Neither list shows a tab of a private or deleted profile |
| AR-10 | Browsing history view | P1 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | – | History is a page in a tab, as D39 planned once internal pages existed: orbit://history/ shows every visit of the tab's profile from the history store, newest first by day, virtualised and paged, with search (all words, title or address). ⌘Y (Ctrl+H), Archive → View History (macOS) and the command bar's View History show the History tab of the Space the window shows (the one used last), else open one; an open Library makes way; from a Mini Window it shows in the latest main window. The list loads again each time its tab shows again. A row opens its page in a new tab (⌘-click or middle-click: behind); its × or its menu (Open in New Tab, Open in Background, Copy Link, Remove from History) removes every visit to the page. The page asks main only about its own tab's profile and opens only pages it listed (D53). The Library keeps its History section, the same list. Clearing the Archive leaves history alone |
| AR-11 | Sidebar backups and "Restore Data" | P2 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | – | Backups of the whole sidebar (Spaces, each profile’s Favorites, pinned and Today tabs, folders, split views; no private profiles) in userData/backups, one JSON file each: taken within 5 minutes of a sidebar change (only when it differs from the newest; browsing alone never makes one), once 30 s after launch, before every restore, and with Back Up Now. Kept: the newest 10 of today, then the newest of each of the 10 days before, of each week of the month before that and of each 30 days of the year before that; a deleted profile’s Favorites, Spaces and tabs are taken out of every backup. Help → Restore Data… (macOS) and the command bar open the Backups section of the Library: a dated list (day headings, time, Spaces and tabs; a file that can’t be read is listed as such, without Restore); Restore… asks first, then puts the sidebar back: tabs in both keep their page, tabs only in the backup come back asleep (with the page and history the Archive kept for them, leaving the Archive), tabs opened since go to the Archive, Spaces added since go; private windows and their tabs are left alone; Favorites over 12 go to Today (D33). When the sidebar can’t be backed up first, nothing changes. A running import stops first: none of the tabs it hasn’t shown yet go to the Archive, and its window says why (D65). Each restore is one step on the sidebar’s undo stack (TB-18): the toast’s Undo or ⌘Z, also in the Library, puts back the sidebar it replaced, a second ⌘Z goes further back and ⌘⇧Z restores again; earlier steps stay. After an undo, a window moved off a removed Space stays where it went, and the pages come back asleep |

| KS-02 | Conflicts with web pages ("prefer websites" vs "prefer Orbit") | P0 | 🟡 partial | ✅ e2e+unit | – | who gets a key first, per action: on Windows and Linux Toggle Sidebar (Ctrl+S, SB-11) and Copy URL (Ctrl+Shift+C, NV-17) prefer websites; every other action, and on macOS every action, ⌘S included (D60), prefers Orbit (the page never sees the key); with prefer websites the page gets the first press: left alone, the action runs; used (preventDefault), a toast offers the action and a second press within a second runs it; a held key's repeats stay the page's; with the keyboard in a frame, that frame says what it did; no answer within 250 ms counts as left alone (D60), so a busy page holds a key a quarter of a second at most; while a page's main frame loads, Orbit takes the keys at once (Electron runs no isolated-world script in a loading page); Settings → Shortcuts sets it per action (right-click → Prefer Websites / Prefer Orbit; a “Websites first” tag on the row); Esc leaving window full screen (NV-20) prefers websites by default: the page gets the first press, and pressing it again within a second or holding it leaves; Settings → Shortcuts' Exit Full Screen row sets it, and with prefer Orbit one Esc leaves at once (D68); a page's Esc gets no toast, as nothing asks the page; Esc leaving a video's own full screen keeps Chromium's rule; nothing holds Cmd+E yet |

| KS-05 | Tabs and windows | P0 | 🟡 partial | ✅ e2e+unit | – | ⌘N, ⌘⇧N, ⌘⌥N, ⌘W / Ctrl+W / Ctrl+F4, ⌘⇧W / Ctrl+Shift+W (closes the window, or the Mini Window, Settings or onboarding window that has focus; Alt+F4 is the system's), ⌘⇧T (a closed tab comes back in its place), ⌘D (pins; again, back to the top of Today), ⌘⇧C, ⌘⇧⌥C, ⌘S, ⌘⇧K, ⌘⇧E, F6 (keyboard between the sidebar and the page), tested from a page; Duplicate Tab, Reset Tab, Rename Tab (shows a hidden sidebar to edit the name), Archive Tab, Move Tab to Space… (the command bar on its Move to rows) and Favorite This Tab have no keys until the user gives them some; ⌘Z (sidebar undo) is not remappable yet; the blank window (⌃⌘N, TB-17) and the top toolbar (⌘⇧D, SB-17) are not built |

No action can take these keys, nor Alt+F4, Alt+Tab or Alt+F on Windows and Linux, and Settings → Shortcuts says what keeps them (KS-03). Windows and Linux: Alt+F4 closes the window and, on the last one, quits; F1 opens Help (OB-13) and can’t be changed there. An Exit item comes with the Windows/Linux app menu (SB-26, not built). The menu template and keymap are unit-tested; not run on a Mac |

Known limits: with the keyboard in a frame of a loading page, Esc stops the load after 250 ms, as only the main frame says whether it used Esc (K5); the first key right after the keyboard moves into a frame can come before that frame says where its keyboard is: Back and Forward then run at once, even in a field that uses them, and a prefer-websites key acts after 250 ms (K7) |
| KS-17 | Mouse, trackpad and modifier-click bindings | P0 | 🟡 partial | ✅ e2e | – | each pointer binding checked against its feature's tests: ⌘-click or middle-click, ⇧⌘-, ⇧- (Peek), ⌥- (split view) and ⌘⌥-click (Mini Window) on links; ⌘-click or middle-click on Back, Forward (keys e2e) or Reload for a new tab; long-press or right-click Back / Forward for history; double-click Reload to stop; ⌘-click a pinned tab's favicon (PN-04); ⌘- / ⇧-click rows (TB-13); double-click the empty sidebar (keys e2e), a tab row (TB-12) or a Favorite (FV-06); swipe over the sidebar (SP-08); pinch / ⌘-scroll (NV-06); mouse buttons 4/5; right-click twice on a video (MD-02). Not built: ⌘-hover + New Tab to paste and go (CB-12), swipe over the page (NV-02), ⌥-click Capture full page (DT-09) |
| KS-18 | Shortcut hints everywhere | P1 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | – | button tooltips (address, copy link, site controls, sidebar toggle, back/forward/reload, find, zoom, Library, Clear, Space dots, Peek, Mini Window Open in…), the empty-window hint, command-bar rows, macOS menu items, the shortcut sheet (OB-12) and the right-click menus of a tab, a multi-selection, the page and a split pane (an item that does what a key does shows that key’s first binding) follow a remap without a restart; a menu shows it the next time it opens. Windows and Linux have no app menu yet (SB-03, SB-26), so there is no menu bar there to label |
| KS-19 | Keys inside overlays | P0 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | – | the open overlay takes its keys first: command bar (⌘T/⌘L/⌘W/Esc), find bar (Enter/⇧Enter/Esc, NV-05), Peek (Esc, ⌘O, ⌘W, PK-09; Esc closes the Peek and the tab under it keeps loading), the recent-tab switcher (Tab/⇧Tab/`, W, letting go of ⌃), permission prompt and site controls (Esc), the sidebar with keyboard focus (arrows, Enter, Esc back to the page, SB-22); then Esc on a loading page goes to the page first: the page's preload tells main whether the page used it, and Orbit stops the load only if it didn't, waiting 250 ms at most (no answer counts as left alone; D59, D60); only the main frame of a tab's page answers, and only for an Esc pressed there; in window full screen Esc goes to the page first, and held or pressed twice leaves full screen (NV-20); the print dialog: Esc closes it wherever its keyboard is, the preview included, Enter prints and Tab stays inside it (NV-07) |
| KS-20 | Shortcuts in special windows | P1 | 🟡 partial | ✅ e2e+unit | – | private window: the same keys, but the actions that need Spaces, pinned tabs, Favorites, folders or the Archive (⌘D, ⌃1–9 / Alt+1–9, ⌘⌥← / ⌘⌥→, ⌘⇧K Clear, Favorite, New Folder, View Archive, every Space action) do nothing there, from a key, a menu or the command bar, and a toast says “Not available in a private window”; its sidebar has no Clear button; tab keys work. Mini Window: ⌘W closes it, ⌘O / ⌘⌥O move or offer to move its page (KS-10), ⌘L edits its address with the keyboard in the field and Esc gives the keyboard back to its page, ⌘R, zoom and print act on its page, sidebar and Space keys do nothing; ⌘Y / Ctrl+H History, the Library and Help → Keyboard Shortcuts open in the browser window behind it. Full screen: every key works with the sidebar hidden; ⌘1–9 and ⌘⌥↑ / ⌘⌥↓ switch tabs without bringing it out. Not built: ⌘F in a Mini Window (it has no find bar, Mini Window lane), the blank window (TB-17), extension keys in private windows (EX-06, EX-10) |

| DT-01 | Open / close DevTools | P0 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | – | ⌥⌘I / F12 (Ctrl+Shift+I / F12) open DevTools for the selected tab or focused split pane, docked inside its view, and close them, also from inside DevTools; a Peek's or Mini Window's page gets its own. ⌥⌘J (Ctrl+Shift+J) opens them on the Console; View → Developer menu (macOS) and the command bar. A key held down acts once. Copy, paste (after DevTools' own paste warning) and the device toolbar work; links DevTools open become tabs. Windows/Linux: while DevTools have the keyboard, only the DevTools keys reach Orbit |

Picker: ⌥⌘C on macOS, no default key on Windows/Linux, Inspect Element in the command bar. ⇧⌘C stays Copy URL; inside DevTools it is DevTools' own picker. Remap: give the devtools.inspect action ⇧⌘C (and take it from tab.copyUrl) in src/shared/actions.ts, or in Settings → Shortcuts once remapping (ST-08) lands |
| DT-03 | DevTools docking, size and focus | P1 | ✅ | ✅ e2e | – | docked right/left/bottom or undocked from DevTools' dock menu; the engine keeps the side per profile across restarts. Each tab (pane, Peek, Mini Window) has its own DevTools, shown and hidden with its page; a page shown again takes the docked size last chosen. Undocked: the open key brings them to the front (checked on Linux; macOS unverified), and closes them when they have the keyboard. No windows added, however many tabs have DevTools. What Orbit puts over a page (find bar, zoom, link pill, loading indicator, permission prompt) goes over the page's own area, never over docked DevTools (e2e for the find bar and link pill, docked right, bottom and left) |
| DT-04 | View page source | P1 | ✅ | ✅ e2e | – | ⌥⌘U (Ctrl+U), the command bar's View Source, the page menu's View Page Source and View → Developer → View Source (macOS menu) open the page's own address as view-source: in a new tab, shown at once: the engine's source view, read-only, coloured, with line numbers; a Peek's page opens its own source in a new tab of its window, and a Mini Window's in a main window (one showing its Space if there is one), brought to the front; a source view has no source of its own to open. Only the page's own address goes, so a web page can't make Orbit open a file: URL this way (D49) |
| DT-05 | Developer mode turns on automatically for local development URLs | P1 | – | – | – |  |
| DT-06 | Turn Developer mode on/off for any site | P1 | – | – | – |  |
| DT-07 | Developer mode appearance and toolbar | P1 | – | – | – |  |

| DT-09 | Showcase screenshot | P2 | – | – | – |  |
| DT-10 | Show full URL outside Developer mode | P1 | – | – | – |  |
| DT-11 | Task manager (per-tab memory/CPU) | P1 | – | – | – |  |
| DT-12 | Record a performance trace (local) | P2 | – | – | – |  |
| DT-13 | Internal pages for engine-level settings | P1 | 🟡 partial | ✅ e2e+unit | – | orbit://<page>/ opens as a normal tab when typed in the command bar or address field, or from another internal page's link; orbit://pages/ lists them; orbit://version/ shows the build info About shows (Orbit, build day, Electron, Chromium, V8, Node, OS) with Copy build info. orbit://history/ is History (AR-10, pages lane). They follow the app's state (light/dark) through the same bridge as Orbit's UI, which the one web page preload (src/preload/page.ts) gives an orbit: page's main frame only (D40, D53). A web page can't navigate, frame, redirect to, open, load or fetch them, and gets no bridge: Orbit opens one for no page but another internal page on any route (the page menu, Split View's item included, ⌥-click, new tabs, windows and pop-ups, a pop-up's own, blocked pop-ups, a drop), D53. Each page runs only the commands listed for it and sends no events, and its document runs only its own scripts (script-src 'self'), D53. Infrastructure documented for reuse (D39) in src/main/devtools/internal-pages.ts and src/renderer/src/internal/registry.ts: a page is a *.internal-page.tsx module, and lists the commands it runs in INTERNAL_PAGE_COMMANDS. Missing: the pages other lanes add as they build them (D54): extensions EX-07, site settings OT-07/ST-13, privacy and clearing data and system options ST-12, languages ST-14, about UP-07; orbit://pages/ lists each one added |
| DT-14 | Hard reload and cache-bypassing reload | P1 | ✅ | ✅ e2e | – | ⇧⌘R (Ctrl+Shift+R) runs the navigation lane's nav.hardReload action (the e2e checks that action ran): page and subresources refetched (no-cache). A crashed page hands the keyboard to the window, so ⇧⌘R brings it back. Stopping a load (Esc in the page, double-clicking Reload) is NV-04, built with the sidebar's Reload/Stop button; its e2e tests cover both |

Programs, installers, scripts and disk images wait under their partial name with Keep / Discard in the sidebar row, the Library and the flyout, through a restart too: everywhere exe, msi, dmg, pkg, deb, rpm, AppImage, .desktop launchers, sh/bash/zsh/py/pl/rb scripts, iso/img/vhd/vhdx, jar, jnlp, apk…; on Windows also its own script, shortcut and system types (js, vbs, wsf, hta, lnk, url, scf, settingcontent-ms, chm, reg, inf, msc, dll…). Keep puts the file in place and marks it, Discard deletes it. Every such file is held, whatever the site, as there is no reputation service. Gap, by the spec's own rule (D54): Safe Browsing, which needs a reputation service; none is free to use (Google's is non-commercial, Web Risk is paid) |

Missing: offering Orbit as Windows' app for local .pdf files (Settings → General, P2), which finish-settings builds (D54): the installer's file association and opening files passed on the command line |

The command bar has a "Downloads" action |
| DL-15 | Pause, resume and retry | P1 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | – | Pause/Resume from the row's menu (and a Resume button on a paused row); a cut-off download shows Resume when the server sent an ETag or Last-Modified (continues with a range request), else Retry (starts again); one cut off by quitting resumes after a restart from its partial file (kept under a hidden second name while the engine shuts down). Downloads never block the tab that started them |
| DL-16 | Downloads in private windows, Little windows and Peek | P2 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | – | Peek and Mini Window downloads go to the same list as any other. A private window's downloads save to disk like any other but are in no saved list (not the downloads list, nor the state file or its backup), and their Windows Zone.Identifier names no address. A private window shows only its own session's downloads (sidebar row, Ctrl+J flyout), and no other window shows them; their start, toasts and the files Orbit opens stay in its windows, and they change nothing kept (the Library's section, the Dock's notification names no file). They stay listed while a private window is open, its pages closed or not; when the last one closes (the session ends), they leave every list: finished files stay on disk, one still coming is saved and then leaves, a paused or stopped one and a program held back (DL-12) are discarded. Tested with real private windows |
| DL-17 | Dock / taskbar progress | P2 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | – | While downloads run or are paused, their overall progress shows on the macOS Dock icon and on the windows' taskbar buttons: bytes received of those with a known size, the can't-tell bar when no size is known, Windows' paused colour when every one is paused; it goes when none runs. A download that finishes while no Orbit window has focus bounces the Dock icon once (macOS) and shows a "Download complete" notification naming the file (a private window's isn't named). Tests read what Orbit asks of the OS through test hooks; the OS's own drawing isn't checked on Linux |
| DL-18 | Smart renaming of downloads | OOS | ⛔ out of scope | – | – | the spec leaves it out |

## Import of data from other browsers

Spec: `spec/import.md`

| ID | Feature | P | Built | Tested | Feels right | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| IM-01 | Import entry points | P1 | 🟡 partial | ✅ e2e | – | the import window (a child of the browser window, in its Space's colours): Back / Next / Cancel, Cancel at any step imports nothing, Enter is Next and Escape is Back, ⌘W closes it. Opened from onboarding (the same flow inline, OB-03), the command bar's Import from Another Browser, Settings → General → Import…, and on macOS the app menu's Import from Another Browser… (macOS-unverified). Not built: a ☰ entry on Windows/Linux (Orbit has no ☰ menu). In the progress view, Cancel is offered only while the source is read; once adding starts it offers Hide, and the bookmarks added are one undo step. The window isn’t modal: the browser window stays usable while it’s open, as IM-14 asks |
| IM-02 | Choose the source browser and profile(s) | P1 | 🟡 partial | ✅ e2e+unit | – | the browsers found on this computer (Chrome, Chromium, Brave, Edge, Vivaldi, Opera, Opera GX, Firefox; Safari on macOS), each a tile in its colour with its profile or profile count; those not installed aren't shown. Several profiles: a step to choose one or more, by name. Profiles come from Chromium's Local State (or a single Default folder, or Opera's own folder) and Firefox's profiles.ini; every file is read from a copy. Safari without Full Disk Access is shown as blocked, with the way round it (export a bookmarks file from Safari and import that). Tests search only made-up fixture folders. Letter tiles, not logos: Orbit doesn't ship other browsers' marks. Safari's reader (Bookmarks.plist, a binary property list) is tested on fixtures, macOS-unverified |
| IM-03 | Choose which data types to import | P1 | 🟡 partial | ✅ e2e+unit | – | after the source and its profiles, what they hold as checkboxes, all on, with counts ("6 bookmarks, as pinned tabs", "6 pages visited"); types a source can't provide aren't shown, and a profile whose file the browser holds offers the rest; never passwords or cards (D52). Cancel (Do this later in onboarding) weighs the same as Next. Extensions are listed, off, as not importable yet (IM-09). Cookies (IM-10) aren’t offered. A file that is there but can’t be read is named with why, e.g. “Work: history couldn’t be read (the file is damaged)”, and the profile’s other types are still offered |
| IM-04 | Choose which bookmarks to import | P1 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | – | the source's tree (Chromium's bookmarks bar, other and mobile bookmarks; Firefox's toolbar, menu, other and mobile bookmarks; Safari's favorites bar, menu and reading list; a file's own groups), several profiles each under its name, with a checkbox per folder and bookmark; everything chosen at first; Select all / none; "4 of 6 bookmarks selected". Addresses that can't be pinned show unticked with the reason. Folders below the top level start closed, and so does a top-level one holding over 1,000 bookmarks. The list isn’t virtualized: every row at the top level or in an open folder is drawn, so a large file shows quickly only when its bookmarks sit in such closed folders (20,000 in folders of 2,000 show in about 0.4 s). 20,000 bookmarks at the top level take about 2.9 s to show; 200,000 there, or 200 top-level folders of 1,000, about 30 s; 10,000 top-level folders about 6 s; and opening a large folder draws all its rows. Only the import window waits |
| IM-05 | Mapping bookmarks into Orbit (pinned tabs and folders) | P1 | 🟡 partial | ✅ e2e+unit | – | one pinned folder "Imported from <Browser>" ("Imported bookmarks" from a file) at the end of the target Space's pinned section: the source's top-level groups and nested folders kept, in order, as closed sub-folders (the folder itself closed above 1,000 items); several profiles into one Space each get a sub-folder by name; each bookmark a pinned tab with its title and address, asleep, with no favicon or request until opened; bookmarklets, saved searches, browser-only and non-web addresses skipped and counted; Firefox tags and separators left out; no Favorites made; one undo step takes it all back. 2,000 bookmarks take about 0.3–0.4 s, made out of sight in parts and shown at once (IM-14), with the longest main-process stall about 40–50 ms. Not built: fetching a favicon when an imported row scrolls into view; its icon comes when the tab is first opened |
| IM-06 | Target Space and profile for imported data | P1 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | – | the last step: the profile (it gets the history) and the Space (its pinned section gets the bookmarks): the current Space by default, the first one in onboarding, or New Space… with a name. Several source profiles: "Make a matching Orbit profile and Space for each" makes them, in order, named after the source profiles, each getting its own profile's history. Private windows' profiles aren't offered and never get history |
| IM-07 | History import | P1 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | – | Chromium's History, Firefox's places.sqlite and Safari's History.db (macOS-unverified), read from copies a window of rows at a time, into the chosen profile's history: each page with its title, visit and typed counts and its newest visits (up to 20). History (⌘Y / Ctrl+H) lists them and the command bar suggests and completes them at once; no tab is made and nothing loads. Left out: browsers' own pages, hidden pages, frame loads (Chromium subframes; Firefox embeds, framed links, downloads). History keeps the 50,000 most recent pages: a larger history keeps its newest and the summary counts the rest. 100,000 pages take about 2 s, with main's longest stall about 50–110 ms and none in the windows; the profile's history is written once, as a snapshot |
| IM-08 | Password import | P1 | ⛔ out of scope | – | – | Orbit has no password manager to import into: the spec has no row for one (OT-11), and Electron has none. IM-03 offers no Passwords type, and IM-12 and IM-13 take no passwords CSV (D52) |
| IM-09 | Extension import (Chromium-family sources) | P1 | 🟡 partial | ✅ e2e+unit | – | A Chromium-family profile's extensions are listed on the types step, from its Preferences and Secure Preferences (read from copies; a name kept only in the manifest is read from it, in its default language): pinned ones first, the browser's own left out. The row is off and says they aren't importable yet; unpacked ones never come over. Not built: installing them fresh from the store with one summary confirmation, pinning the pinned ones, and the ad-blocker de-duplication (blockers are already marked), because the extensions lane's install path isn't on main yet. Firefox add-ons aren't listed (the spec covers Chromium-family sources) |
| IM-10 | Cookies / signed-in sessions import | P2 | – | – | – |  |
| IM-11 | Autofill addresses and payment cards import | P2 | ⛔ out of scope | – | – | Orbit has no store for addresses and cards to import into: the spec has no row for one (OT-12), and Electron has none (D52) |
| IM-12 | Bringing data over from a browser Orbit can’t read (user-facing exports only) | P1 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | – | Paste a list of links (one address per line, "Title — address" with a dash, bar or tab, Markdown links, bullets): one pinned folder named by the user, a pinned tab per link in order, asleep; lines that aren't links are counted in the summary. ⌘V / Ctrl+V on the sidebar (outside a text field) with two or more links on the clipboard opens the same import with them filled in. A list over about 1 MB or 10,000 lines, pasted or from a file, isn’t put in the text field: the import window shows its count and first eight lines, read-only, with Clear, and imports it as it is. A paste over 64 MB as UTF-8 (22.5 million CJK characters, say) says “This is too large to import (the limit is 64 MB)”, as a file does, and none of it leaves the window it was pasted in. Clear also frees main’s copy of a held list. The other routes (a bookmarks file, notes, canvases, site styles) are explained in the import window's help, which reads nothing from another browser; passwords are out of scope (D52) |
| IM-13 | Import from files (standard formats) | P1 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | – | bookmarks HTML (the Netscape format; Chromium- and Firefox-style exports tested) and a .txt list of links, from From a file… or dropped on the import window or the sidebar. Bookmarks map as IM-05 into "Imported bookmarks"; links as IM-12 (a list over about 1 MB or 10,000 lines shows only its count and first lines); a file with neither says "No bookmarks found in this file" and imports nothing; a cut-off file imports what it holds. Files are read in a worker, in time linear in their size (D58): main’s longest stall is about 0.07 s for a 16 MB file or list, and about 0.2 s for a 60 MB file of 200,000 bookmarks. A file nested deeper than 64 folders keeps its deeper bookmarks in the 64th; a file gives at most 200,000 bookmarks (folders don’t count) and 20,000 folders, the bookmarks of folders past that kept in the folder that holds them; over 64 MB, every route, a paste included, says “This is too large to import (the limit is 64 MB)” without reading it; a read that fails says “Orbit couldn’t read this file”. No passwords CSV (D52) |
| IM-14 | Progress, summary and errors | P1 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | – | progress per data type (a spinner, then a check), then a summary with counts per type and the skipped items with reasons; Done shows the imported folder in the sidebar (its Space, the pinned section open, the folder in view). Bookmarks are made out of sight, in parts, and their folder is shown whole, at once (D62): while 20,000 are added, the browser window’s longest freeze is under 0.1 s; 100,000 take about 34 s, with the window’s longest freeze about 0.34 s and main’s longest stall about 0.57 s (saving the state). A file the source browser holds (it can't be copied) shows "Chrome is using some of its files. Quit Chrome and try again, or import the rest" with Try again; the types it could read can still be imported. History shows the pages read, then added; Done says they're in History and the command bar; what History can't keep is listed with the reason. The summary lists every item left out with its reason: skipped bookmarks (also in a folder that holds nothing else), those past 200,000 bookmarks in one file, list or profile (folders don’t count, so the summary and the selection count agree), lines that aren’t links, and a profile’s file that couldn’t be read (“Work: history couldn’t be read (the file is damaged)”). Until the folder shows, nothing lists its tabs (D65): not the command bar (by title, by address or among recent tabs), the recent-tab switcher or the Library. One the user reached anyway and placed stays where they put it, and the folder leaves it out. A quit or a failure part-way takes back exactly the tabs the import made, by id, wherever they are, and nothing of the user’s; a crash part-way leaves none either, as the next start removes tabs that no section shows. Restore Data part-way stops the import first: its tabs are removed without going to the Archive, and the import window says “The import stopped: data was restored from a backup.” Copies of the other browser’s files go in a folder under Orbit’s user data, removed at quit (a copy still being made too) and cleared at startup (D58) |
| IM-15 | Re-import and duplicates | P2 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | – | the same browser or file again makes a new "Imported from <Browser> (2)" folder (then (3)…), never merging into or changing the first. History de-duplicates silently: a page already imported gains only the visits it lacked, so its counts aren't doubled. Passwords aren't imported (D52) |
| IM-16 | Starter suggestions from imported history | P2 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | – | after onboarding's import of a history, the Done step offers the six sites visited most (each by its most-visited page, or its home page when that's a search): the first three as Favorites, the rest as pinned tabs. One click takes one (another takes it back); Dismiss all drops them. They're added unloaded with the import when Start browsing ends onboarding, never with Skip setup (D44). Orbit can't tell web apps from other sites, so it ranks by visits; a suggested pinned tab is named after its site until first opened |
| IM-17 | Export Orbit's pinned items (anti-lock-in) | P2 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | – | Export Pinned Items as Bookmarks… in the File menu (macOS-unverified: Orbit has no menu bar elsewhere), the command bar, and Settings → General → Import and export (with Include Today tabs) writes a standard bookmarks HTML file through the system's save dialog: the Favorites a folder (one per profile when there are several), each Space a folder of its pinned section with its folders nested as they are, a split's tabs in its place; Today's tabs only when chosen, as a Today folder in their Space. Orbit's own pages and private windows' profiles are left out. Copy All Links on a folder is the tabs lane's (it exists) |
